q: Which club plays its home games at Anfield?
sub: Everton played there first, from 1884 until a rent row in 1892.

q: Which club plays its home games at Old Trafford?
sub: The ground opened on 19 February 1910, and Liverpool won the first match 4-3.

q: Which club plays its home games at Stamford Bridge?
sub: The ground opened in 1877 for the London Athletic Club, and the club was founded later to fill it.

q: Which club plays its home games at the Etihad Stadium?
sub: They moved in during the summer of 2003.

q: Which club plays its home games at St James' Park?
sub: Football has been played on the site since 1880.

q: Which club plays its home games at Villa Park?
sub: The first match there was a friendly against Blackburn Rovers in April 1897.

q: Which club played at Goodison Park until 2025?
sub: The last men's match there was a 2-0 win over Southampton on 18 May 2025.

q: Which club plays its home games at Molineux?
sub: Named after Benjamin Molineux, who bought the land in 1744.

q: Which club plays its home games at Craven Cottage, on the bank of the Thames?
sub: The Cottage itself is a pavilion in the corner, built in 1905.

q: Which south London club plays its home games at Selhurst Park?
sub: The ground opened in August 1924 and they lost the first game there 1-0.

q: Which club plays its home games at the King Power Stadium?
sub: Gary Lineker performed the opening ceremony in July 2002.

q: Which ground did Arsenal leave in 2006 when they moved to the Emirates Stadium?
sub: Officially Arsenal Stadium, home from 1913 after the club moved north from Plumstead.

q: Which ground did Tottenham Hotspur leave in 2017?
sub: Their home for 118 years, from 1899.

q: Which club moved into the London Stadium, built for the 2012 Olympics, in 2016?
sub: They signed a 99-year lease on the place in March 2013.

q: Which ground did Sunderland move into in 1997?
sub: Built on the site of Wearmouth Colliery, and named for the miners' Davy lamps.

q: What is the famous home end at Anfield called?
sub: Named by a local journalist after a Boer War hill where British troops died.

q: Which end at Old Trafford traditionally holds Manchester United's loudest support?
sub: It was the last stand at the ground to be given a roof, and the last to be seated.

q: Which club has a cannon on its crest?
sub: From the Royal Arsenal armaments works in Woolwich, where the club started in 1886.

q: Which club has a liver bird on its crest?
sub: The city's symbol. It flew on a flag over Anfield as early as September 1892.

q: Which colour shirts do Leeds United wear at home?
sub: Don Revie switched them to all white in 1961-62 to look like Real Madrid.

q: Which ground did Manchester City leave in 2003?
sub: Their home for 80 years, from 1923.

q: Which ground did Southampton leave in 2001 when they moved to St Mary's Stadium?
sub: The site is now a housing estate with blocks named after old Saints players.

q: Which ground did West Ham United leave in 2016?
a: The Boleyn Ground, also known as Upton Park
sub: Boleyn because a nearby house was called Boleyn Castle, after Anne Boleyn.

q: Which ground did Leicester City leave in 2002?
sub: Their home for 111 years. The new ground went up 200 yards away.

q: Which ground did Sunderland leave in 1997?
sub: It hosted four matches at the 1966 World Cup.

q: What was the King Power Stadium called when it opened in 2002?
sub: The crisp firm had a ten-year naming deal. King Power took over in July 2011.

q: What was the Etihad Stadium called before the 2011 sponsorship deal?
sub: Also known as Eastlands while it was being built.

q: Which sporting event was Manchester City's Etihad Stadium originally built for?
sub: It held 38,000 for the Games, with a running track that was later dug out.

q: Which club plays its home games at the bet365 Stadium?
sub: They moved in during 1997, to a site at Trentham Lakes.

q: What was the bet365 Stadium called before it was renamed in 2016?
sub: It opened on 30 August 1997, named after a building society.

q: Which club plays its home games at The Hawthorns?
sub: It was the sixth ground the club had used when they moved in, in 1900.

q: Which club plays its home games at Ewood Park?
sub: Jack Walker's steel fortune paid for the rebuild in the early 1990s.

q: Which club plays its home games at Carrow Road?
sub: The whole ground was put up in 82 days in 1935.

q: Which club plays its home games at Fratton Park?
sub: Blue shirts, white shorts and red socks, the socks added after the war as a memorial.

q: Which club plays its home games at the Riverside Stadium?
sub: It opened in August 1995.

q: Which club plays its home games at Kenilworth Road?
sub: Their home since 1905, and the away end is reached through a row of terraced houses.

q: Which club plays its home games at Vicarage Road?
sub: Saracens rugby club shared it from 1997 to 2013.

q: What is Chelsea's traditional home end at Stamford Bridge called?
sub: Supporters nicknamed the 1930 south terrace the Shed and the club adopted it.

q: Which end at St James' Park is named after the city's old gallows?
sub: At the other end is the Leazes End, named after Leazes Park.

q: Which end at Villa Park is named after a former owner of Aston Hall?
sub: Sir Thomas Holte. The pitch sits on what was once his kitchen garden.

q: Which club has a cockerel standing on a ball on its crest?
sub: Harry Hotspur dug in his spurs, and spurs belong on a fighting cock.

q: Which bird sits on a football on the Norwich City crest?
sub: A chairman who bred canaries gave the club the nickname and the yellow kit.

q: Which club switched to red shirts in 1902, when it stopped being called Newton Heath?
sub: Newton Heath had played in white with blue cord.

q: Which Liverpool manager put the team in an all-red kit in 1964?
sub: Red for danger, red for power. Before that it was red shirts and white shorts.

q: Which electronics company sponsored Manchester United's shirts from 1982 to 2000?
sub: Vodafone took over for the 2000-01 season.

q: Which club did Arsenal beat 4-2 in the last match at Highbury in May 2006?
sub: The win took fourth place off Tottenham on the final day.

q: Who scored a hat-trick in Arsenal's final match at Highbury in 2006?
sub: He kissed the turf afterwards.

q: What was built on the site of Highbury after Arsenal left?
a: Flats, in a development called Highbury Square
sub: 711 apartments. The listed Art Deco East Stand front was kept, and the pitch is a garden.

q: Which club beat Manchester City 1-0 in the last match at Maine Road in May 2003?
sub: Michael Svensson scored the ground's last goal.

q: Which Southampton player scored the last competitive goal at The Dell?
sub: A volley off the bench in the closing minutes, to beat Arsenal 3-2 in May 2001.

q: Which club did West Ham United beat 3-2 in the final match at the Boleyn Ground?
sub: Winston Reid scored the winner on 10 May 2016.

q: Who scored the last goal at White Hart Lane, in May 2017?
sub: A consolation. Tottenham beat Manchester United 2-1 to close the ground.

q: Where did Tottenham Hotspur play their home league games in 2017-18?
sub: The new ground was not ready, so they spent a whole season there.

q: Who scored the first competitive goal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, in April 2019?
sub: Crystal Palace were beaten 2-0.

q: Which two clubs have groundshared at Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park?
sub: Charlton from 1985 to 1991, Wimbledon from 1991 to 2003.

q: Where did Fulham play from 2002 to 2004 while Craven Cottage was being rebuilt?
sub: Two seasons as lodgers at Queens Park Rangers.

q: Which club played at Anfield before Liverpool existed?
sub: They fell out with landlord John Houlding in 1892, left for Goodison, and he founded Liverpool.

q: Where did Manchester United play home games from 1941 to 1949, after Old Trafford was bombed?
sub: They rented Manchester City's ground for £5,000 a year plus a cut of the gate.

q: Which stand at Old Trafford was renamed after Sir Alex Ferguson in 2011?
sub: Renamed on 5 November 2011, marking 25 years in the job.

q: Which Chelsea director, killed in a helicopter crash in 1996, has a Stamford Bridge stand named after him?
sub: His money rebuilt the club in the early 1990s.

q: What was Bolton Wanderers' Reebok Stadium renamed in 2014?
sub: Then the University of Bolton Stadium in 2018, then the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

q: Which ground, 551 feet above sea level, was the highest used by any English league club?
sub: West Bromwich Albion's home sits higher than any other Football League or Premier League ground.

q: Which ground did Stoke City leave in 1997, after 119 years?
sub: It was the oldest ground in the Football League when it was pulled down.

q: Which ground did Derby County leave in 1997 for Pride Park?
sub: Francis Ley built it for baseball for his foundry workers, hence the name.

q: Which ground was the first in England to have permanent floodlights, installed in 1950?
sub: The first game under them was against Bournemouth on 31 October 1950.

q: Which club adopted red and blue striped shirts in 1973, inspired by Barcelona?
sub: Malcolm Allison's overhaul. Before that they played in claret and blue.

q: Which club has a song thrush perched on a hawthorn branch on its crest?
sub: A throstle is a song thrush, and the branch came in after they moved to The Hawthorns.

q: Which manager put Leeds United in an all-white kit, copying Real Madrid?
sub: From 1961-62. Before that they had worn blue and gold.

q: Which company's name was on Liverpool's shirts when they won the 2019-20 Premier League?
sub: The bank took over from Carlsberg, who had been there from 1992 to 2010.

q: Which ground hosted a 1966 World Cup semi-final, the only one ever played at an English club ground?
sub: West Germany beat the Soviet Union 2-1 there on 25 July 1966.

q: The record Premier League attendance of 83,222 was set at Wembley in February 2018. Which two clubs played?
sub: Spurs won 1-0 during their season away from home.

q: The lowest Premier League attendance, 3,039, came at Selhurst Park in January 1993. Which club were at home?
sub: They lost 3-1 to Everton. Their average that season was 8,353, also a low.

q: Which Leicester City player scored the last goal at Filbert Street, in May 2002?
sub: Leicester beat Tottenham 2-1 to close the ground.

q: Which club did Middlesbrough beat 2-0 in the first match at the Riverside Stadium in 1995?
sub: Craig Hignett and Jan Aage Fjortoft scored.

q: Which old ground's gates were re-erected outside Middlesbrough's Riverside Stadium in 2005?
sub: The same gates that were locked when the club went into liquidation in 1986.

q: Which Dutch club played Sunderland in the first match at the Stadium of Light in 1997?
sub: A 0-0 friendly, after Prince Andrew opened the ground.

q: Which ground held the highest average attendance of any Premier League season, 75,821 in 2006-07?
sub: It was also the biggest ground in the league that season.

q: Which club were the visitors for Arsenal's first competitive match at the Emirates Stadium, in 2006?
sub: Gilberto Silva scored Arsenal's first competitive goal at the ground.

q: What was the Emirates Stadium site known as before the naming deal was signed?
sub: Emirates signed a 15-year deal in 2004 worth around £100 million.

q: Which ground was called the Sports Direct Arena between 2011 and 2012?
sub: Newcastle dropped it after a year when Wonga bought the naming rights and gave the name back.

q: Which Norwich City ground was given up after part of the pitch sank into old chalk workings?
sub: One corner dropped as much as 30 feet. Carrow Road replaced it in 1935.

q: Which stand at Elland Road was the largest cantilever stand in the world when it was finished in 1993?
sub: It cost £5.5 million.

q: Which Everton stand was renamed after Howard Kendall in 2016?
sub: It became the Howard Kendall Gwladys Street End that July.

q: What colour shirts were Everton wearing when they moved into Goodison Park in 1892?
a: Salmon pink and dark blue stripes
sub: Royal blue only arrived in 1901-02. They had also tried black with a scarlet sash.

q: Which county cricket club played first-class matches at Sheffield United's Bramall Lane until 1973?
sub: The ground opened for cricket in 1855 and staged 391 first-class matches.

q: The cockerel on the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is a replica, dents and all. Which player shot the original with an air rifle?
sub: The 4.5 metre fibreglass copy on the South Stand reproduces his dents faithfully.

q: Manchester United changed out of their grey kit at half time in 1996, claiming they could not pick each other out. Who were they playing?
sub: The kit was binned after five games. They never won a competitive match in it.

q: Derby County's first competitive match at Pride Park, in August 1997, was abandoned. What went wrong?
sub: They went out eleven minutes into the second half against Wimbledon.

q: Which club wore the Acorns Children's Hospice logo on their shirts, for nothing, in 2008-09 and 2009-10?
sub: The first deal of its kind in the Premier League. Acorns stayed on as charity partner.

q: Griffin Park, Brentford's old ground, was the only English league ground with one of what on each of its four corners?
sub: The Griffin, the Princess Royal, the New Inn and the Brook.
